definition: Ostensible means stated as a reason, but not necessarily the real one.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word ostensible. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know ostensible should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: Her ostensible reason for the 6 a.m. run was training; the bakery along the route told the fuller story.
A declared purpose is simply the one on paper, no wink attached; ostensible raises the eyebrow.
A sham goes past ostensible: ostensible leaves room for the stated reason to be true, while a sham reason is false outright — a costume over the real one.

Professed means declared aloud by the person concerned — a professed pacifist has said so herself, believe it or not. The word points at the act of announcing. Ostensible points at the gap between the reason shown and the reason held, and needs no announcement at all — only a surface.

Purported passes along someone else's claim with a visible shrug — a purported Rembrandt is called that secondhand, by tellers who will not vouch for it. Ostensible is the observer's own cooler verdict on a stated reason: here is the version on display; the truth may sit elsewhere.

Ostendere, 'to show,' does the work — the ostensible motive is the one held up for viewing.
If you know the show is false, sham or pretended says so; ostensible keeps the question politely open.
Ostensible is the reporter's raised eyebrow: it marks the reason shown without ruling on the reason held.
Softer than sham, which convicts, and cooler than supposed, which smirks, it suits filings, motives, and agendas — anywhere the show and the truth might differ.

ostensible: A sham goes past ostensible: ostensible leaves room for the stated reason to be true, while a sham reason is false outright — a costume over the real one.
In April the parks department closed Miller's Pond for what a laminated sign at the gate called habitat restoration, promising the return of nesting turtles.
That was the ostensible reason, and the town newsletter repeated it without comment.
The budget told a different story.
Winter storms had cracked the pond's retaining wall, and the repair estimate ran to eighty thousand dollars the department did not have.
No turtle survey was ever filed.
The restoration contractor listed on the permit turned out to specialize in concrete work.
When the pond reopened two years later, the wall was new, the ledger was balanced, and the sign about turtles was quietly gone.
